**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, § 10 Nonassignability, ¶ p0042).**

**What the document says.** The sole assignment provision is a symmetric consent gate: "Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld."

**Why it fails.** The reasonableness qualifier is helpful, but there is no carve-out letting Clear Capital assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. The playbook fallback requires at least a right to assign to successors, so the clause misses the fallback on a material term — our ability to reorganise or be acquired without RadialSpark's sign-off.

**What is already acceptable (noted, not flagged).**
- No change-of-control language anywhere in the agreement; § 6 termination is limited to convenience when no SOW is outstanding and uncured material breach after 15 days. So there is no Vendor exit or re-pricing right on our change of control — the walk-away trigger is absent.
- The consent standard is mutual and reasonableness-qualified, which already satisfies the second half of the fallback.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** A single in-line proviso to ¶ p0042 adding: Company may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets; and Contractor may not assign or transfer to a competitor of Company. This reaches the preferred position without disturbing the existing mutual consent bargain.
